headline: Sellers Take the Wheel on the First Day of September
body_html:
Tuesday's session opened the historically difficult month of September with a decisive tilt to the downside. Of 549 names in our universe, just 125 finished higher while 421 closed in the red — a lopsided ratio that left little ambiguity about the day's mood. Rising Treasury yields, with the 10-year touching its highest level since January 2025 amid renewed Middle East tensions, gave bears the macro ammunition they needed to press the tape from the opening bell.

The sector picture told a clear rotation story: Energy was the lone bright spot, adding 0.92% as oil prices climbed on geopolitical anxiety. Every other group finished lower, with Software off 2.42% and Semiconductors down 2.36% leading the retreat. Industrials and Homebuilders also suffered notably, the latter squeezed further by mortgage rates surging to their highest since June 2025. The message from the market was unambiguous — money moved toward hard assets and away from growth.

CF Industries stood out as the session's standout mover, jumping 4.28% to pace all gainers, with agriculture peer Corteva adding 3.88%. On the other end, SharkNinja plunged 9.13%, the steepest single-name drop in the universe. Citadel's warning that the risk-reward setup for equities is deteriorating as a seasonally tough stretch begins looks, at least for one day, prescient.

briefs.headline: 10-Year Yield Climbs to 17-Month High on Middle East Flare-Up
briefs.body: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest point since January 2025 as fresh Middle East hostilities pushed investors toward safety in oil and out of rate-sensitive equities. The move rippled directly into Homebuilders, the sector's 1.74% decline reflecting the added pressure of mortgage rates hitting their loftiest level since June 2025.

briefs.headline: AI Trade Hits a Rough Patch as Token Prices Set New Lows
briefs.body: Enthusiasm around artificial intelligence cooled markedly on Tuesday, with AI token prices falling to fresh record lows. The selloff coincided with broad weakness across Software and Semiconductor names, and at least one institutional desk disclosed it was exiting a data-center holding to lock in gains ahead of further turbulence in the theme.

briefs.headline: SharkNinja Suffers Steepest Drop in the Universe
briefs.body: Consumer-products maker SharkNinja shed 9.13% — the largest single-session decline among all 549 names tracked — dragging the broader Consumer sector down 1.63%. The move came on a day when discretionary spending names were broadly out of favor as yields rose and risk appetite faded.

briefs.headline: Credo Technology and Cadence Lead Semis and Software Lower
briefs.body: Connectivity chipmaker Credo Technology fell 8.65% and electronic-design automation firm Cadence Design slid 7.60%, together epitomizing the punishment dealt to technology sub-sectors on Tuesday. The twin declines reflected a broader repricing of AI-linked hardware and software demand assumptions as macro headwinds intensified.

briefs.headline: Eli Lilly Eyes Further Acquisitions With Obesity-Drug Windfall
briefs.body: Pharmaceutical heavyweight Eli Lilly signaled it intends to deploy proceeds from its booming obesity franchise toward additional mergers and acquisitions. The disclosure underscored the bifurcated nature of Tuesday's Healthcare tape, which managed only a modest 0.16% decline even as the rest of the market retreated sharply.

briefs.headline: Congress Races to Avert a Government Shutdown
briefs.body: The U.S. House of Representatives moved to head off a potential government shutdown, though resistance from hardline members within the GOP complicated the path forward. The fiscal uncertainty added another layer of unease to an already difficult session, with traders keeping a close eye on Washington as budget negotiations enter a critical phase.
